text:
Winnipeg arrives on a five-game win streak, the latest an 8-3 romp at Dallas after the Jets trailed by two. They're outscoring opponents 27-14 over the run and have held 60% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in those games, so the wins have real backing. Chicago is 1-4-0 in its last five, but snapped a six-game winless run with an overtime win over Buffalo on Wednesday. The Blackhawks are without Bowen Byram, and Alex Vlasic has stepped up to 22:17 a night from 19:25. Winnipeg won the October meeting 4-3 in overtime, though our numbers say Chicago deserved that one 52% of the time.

Our model leans Winnipeg, 3.25 expected goals to 2.98. The Jets hold 48% of five-on-five expected goals to Chicago's 41%, and they're stronger on the power play (0.83 expected goals per game against 0.49). Chicago's record understates it: a -36 goal difference against -18.4 expected, with finishing and goaltending costing them. In net, projected starters Stuart Skinner (+1.2 goals saved above expected this season, +6.0 last) and Spencer Knight (-1.9 this season, +11.1 last) have swapped places in form.

Kyle Connor is 49% to score and two points shy of 700 for his career. Connor Bedard leads Chicago at 36%. Mark Scheifele has a five-game point streak and ten points in five games against Chicago. Our under-the-radar picks: Brayden Yager, a fourth-liner whose shots have been dangerous (13% to score, 24% for a point), and Roman Kantserov, 58% for a point on a nine-game streak.
